name: mosaic_onecarbon_cycle

executive.question: Does hepatic homocysteine vary across the menstrual cycle with estradiol, and in which direction — as Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021 predict from estradiol activation of the transsulfuration enzyme CBS?
executive.verdict: Yes, inversely. Driving the curated Reed2004 methionine-cycle model with a menstrual-cycle estradiol input and Kim's estradiol activation of CBS, homocysteine falls as estradiol rises — reaching its minimum (~0.6 µM) at the ovulatory E2 peak (~day 12) and its maximum (~1.0 µM) at menstruation (corr(E2, Hcy) ≈ −0.94), reproducing Kim 2021 Fig 2.

scientific_argument: Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021 (PLOS Comput Biol, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009708) extended the Reed/Nijhout one-carbon metabolism models with estradiol-dependent enzyme activation and showed that homocysteine tracks estradiol inversely over the menstrual cycle. The dominant mechanism is estradiol activation of cystathionine-β-synthase (CBS), the transsulfuration enzyme that removes homocysteine: h(E2) = 1 + (E2−0.09)/(0.67+(E2−0.09)). We reproduce this by standing Kim's CBS forcing and a Fourier-fit menstrual E2(t) on top of the curated, retrievable Reed2004 methionine-cycle SBML (BioModels BIOMD0000000698).
title: Kim 2021 one-carbon cycle
claim: Estradiol activation of CBS (transsulfuration) makes hepatic homocysteine vary inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle — lowest at the ovulatory E2 peak — reproducing Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021 on the curated Reed2004 methionine-cycle model.

priors.name: homocysteine_physiological_range
priors.prediction: Over the cycle, hepatic homocysteine should stay in the physiological ~0.5-1.1 µM range (Kim 2021 Fig 2 operating point), not run away.

priors.name: hcy_ovulatory_floor
priors.prediction: At the ovulatory estradiol peak, CBS activation should pull homocysteine to its cycle minimum but not below ~0.5 µM.

priors.name: hcy_menstrual_ceiling
priors.prediction: At menstruation (low estradiol, weak CBS), homocysteine should rise to its cycle maximum but stay below ~1.1 µM.

findings.statement: Hepatic homocysteine varies inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle — minimum at the ovulatory E2 peak, maximum at menstruation — reproducing the central result of Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021.

evidence.observed: corr(E2, Hcy) ≈ -0.94 over the settled cycle; Hcy ≈ 0.60 µM at the day-12 E2 peak vs ≈ 1.03 µM at menstruation (mean 0.72 µM)

expected.summary: Kim 2021 Fig 2 — homocysteine moves opposite to estradiol across the cycle (lowest near ovulation).

findings.explanation: Estradiol activates CBS via h(E2) = 1 + (E2-0.09)/(0.67+(E2-0.09)); higher CBS flux at the E2 peak consumes more homocysteine through transsulfuration, so Hcy falls as E2 rises.

findings.statement: The inverse relationship is driven by estradiol activation of CBS alone — standing Kim's h(E2) forcing on the curated Reed2004 methionine cycle is sufficient to reproduce it.

evidence.observed: with h(E2) on CBS only (no other estradiol targets), Hcy tracks E2 at corr -0.94; the SAM/SAH methylation ratio stays near-flat (methylation homeostasis, Kim 2021 Fig 3A)

expected.summary: Kim 2021 identifies CBS as the dominant estradiol-sensitive node for the homocysteine response.

report.title: Kim 2021 one-carbon cycle
report.objective: Test whether estradiol activation of CBS over the menstrual cycle makes hepatic homocysteine vary inversely with estradiol, reproducing Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021.
report.conclusion: Yes — homocysteine tracks estradiol inversely (corr ≈ -0.94), lowest at the ovulatory E2 peak, built on the curated Reed2004 methionine-cycle SBML plus Kim's exact h(E2) CBS forcing. This is a faithful recreation of the paper's headline (Fig 2), not a de-novo fit.
report.main_insight: The whole menstrual-cycle homocysteine swing follows from a single estradiol target (CBS); the methionine cycle's other fluxes re-balance to keep the SAM/SAH methylation ratio stable.
report.caveat: Methionine-cycle core only (folate pools clamped); Kim's PEMT g(E2) and TS/DHFR u(E2) effects act on folate-cycle enzymes not represented here. E2(t) is a 5-harmonic Fourier fit (peak slightly damped, 1.02 vs 1.15 nM).

conclusion: Estradiol activation of CBS makes hepatic homocysteine vary inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle (corr ≈ -0.94), lowest at the ovulatory E2 peak — a faithful recreation of Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021 on the curated Reed2004 methionine-cycle model.
